templates.name: General
templates.description: Balanced notes for any meeting: overview, topics, decisions, next steps.
templates.instructions: Write neutral, skimmable meeting notes. Prefer concrete nouns and numbers from the call over adjectives. Every decision and next step must cite the lines it came from.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.guidance: 2-3 sentences: purpose of the call and the outcome.

sections.heading: Key topics
sections.guidance: One bullet per topic discussed, in order, with the gist.

sections.heading: Decisions
sections.guidance: Only things explicitly agreed. Omit proposals that weren't settled.

sections.heading: Next steps
sections.guidance: Owner: task (due date if stated).

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.guidance: Unresolved questions someone needs to answer.

templates.name: Product Review
templates.description: For roadmap, scoping and launch discussions.
templates.instructions: Summarize for a product team. Separate customer evidence from opinion. Make trade-offs explicit: what was cut or deferred and why. Quote metrics exactly as stated.

sections.heading: Goals
sections.guidance: What the team is trying to achieve and how success is measured.

sections.heading: Customer signal
sections.guidance: Evidence from customers, sales and support, with numbers.

sections.heading: Decisions
sections.guidance: What was decided, including scope and sequencing.

sections.heading: Scope & trade-offs
sections.guidance: In, out, and deferred - with the reason.

sections.heading: Risks
sections.guidance: Technical, commercial or timeline risks raised.

sections.heading: Launch plan
sections.guidance: Dates, audiences, gates.

sections.heading: Open questions
sections.guidance: Unresolved and who owns the answer.

templates.name: Executive Brief
templates.description: A 60-second read for leadership: outcomes, risks, asks.
templates.instructions: Write for a busy executive who did not attend. Lead with outcomes. No play-by-play. At most 4 bullets per section. Surface anything that needs a leadership decision.

sections.heading: TL;DR
sections.guidance: The 2-3 things that matter.

sections.heading: Decisions made
sections.guidance: Settled outcomes only.

sections.heading: Risks
sections.guidance: What could go wrong and its impact.

sections.heading: Asks & escalations
sections.guidance: What the team needs from leadership.

templates.name: Sales Discovery
templates.description: Qualification notes: pain, requirements, budget, decision process.
templates.instructions: Summarize a sales conversation for the account team and CRM. Use the prospect's own words for pains. Be explicit about unknowns in budget, timeline and decision process - never guess.

sections.heading: Company context
sections.guidance: Who they are, size, team using the product.

sections.heading: Pain points
sections.guidance: Problems in the prospect's words, with impact.

sections.heading: Current solution
sections.guidance: What they use today and why it falls short.

sections.heading: Requirements & objections
sections.guidance: Must-haves, deal blockers, concerns.

sections.heading: Budget & timeline
sections.guidance: Stated budget, timing, triggers.

sections.heading: Decision process
sections.guidance: Champion, economic buyer, steps, competitors.

sections.heading: Next steps
sections.guidance: Agreed follow-ups on both sides.

templates.name: Daily Standup
templates.instructions: One bullet per person per section, prefixed with their name. Keep each under 20 words. Blockers must name who can unblock.

sections.heading: Since last standup
sections.guidance: Completed or progressed work.

sections.heading: Today
sections.guidance: Planned focus.

sections.heading: Blockers
sections.guidance: What's blocked and who can unblock it.

templates.description: Manager/report conversation: wins, concerns, feedback, growth.
templates.instructions: Write private 1:1 notes in a supportive, factual tone. Capture feedback in both directions. Do not editorialize about the person.

sections.heading: Wins
sections.guidance: Recent progress worth recognizing.

sections.heading: Concerns & blockers
sections.guidance: What's worrying or slowing them down.

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.guidance: Feedback given or asked for, both directions.

sections.heading: Growth
sections.guidance: Career goals, stretch opportunities.

sections.heading: Follow-ups
sections.guidance: Commitments from either side.

templates.name: Candidate Interview
templates.description: Structured interview debrief with evidence for each signal.
templates.instructions: Write an interview debrief. Every signal must be backed by what the candidate actually said or did. Separate observation from judgment. End with a recommendation and confidence.

sections.heading: Candidate background
sections.guidance: Relevant experience as described by the candidate.

sections.heading: Technical assessment
sections.guidance: Problem-solving and depth, with evidence.

sections.heading: Communication & collaboration
sections.guidance: How they explained, listened, handled pushback.

sections.heading: Strengths
sections.guidance: Clear positives.

sections.heading: Concerns
sections.guidance: Gaps or risks, with evidence.

sections.heading: Recommendation
sections.guidance: Hire / no hire / next round, with confidence.

calendarEvents.title: Q4 Product Alignment: Insights 2.0
calendarEvents.description: Lock Insights 2.0 scope, beta date, and the SSO vs Jira call. Pre-read: Daniel's one-pager, Priya's eval sheet.
calendarEvents.agenda:
1. Customer signal (Tom, Aisha)
2. Clustering model status (Priya)
3. Capacity (Raj)
4. Themes-first dashboard (Marcus)
5. SSO vs Jira (Daniel)
6. Launch plan (Elena)
7. Owners and dates

attachments.title: SSO vs Jira one-pager (Daniel)
attachments.body:
Recommendation: SAML SSO first (Okta + Azure AD, audit logs), full Jira integration in Q1, one-way "create Jira issue" button now.

Why: $420K ACV (Globex $260K, Arcadia $160K) is blocked on SAML. Jira: 11 accounts asked, ~2 churned.
Effort: SSO 2 engineers x 4-5 weeks. Jira 2 x 4 weeks. Button ~1.5 weeks.
Risks: Azure AD quirks; need real test tenants. SCIM deferred.

attachments.title: Clustering eval sheet (Priya)
attachments.body:
Precision on labeled set (800 comments): August pilot 71% -> re-ranking 78% -> new embeddings 79%. GA bar: 85%.
Failure modes: merged distinct billing problems; overly broad themes ("the app is slow"); ~4% unsupported summary sentences (dropped).
Next: 2,000-comment labeled set incl. retail + healthcare; merge/split feedback from beta.

attachments.title: Dashboard v3 notes (Marcus)
attachments.body: Home = Themes (ranked by volume + growth), 3 quotes per card, neutral trend arrows + sentiment dot, merge/split buttons in theme detail, empty state below ~200 comments with Zendesk import.

calendarEvents.title: Pricing working session: AI features
calendarEvents.agenda: Agree the AI pricing proposal for leadership: options A (Pro + cap), B (add-on), C (per seat).

attachments.title: AI cost model (Helen)
attachments.body: Median workspace: $1.80/month AI cost. Largest pilot: $14/month. ~all cost is theme summaries. Cap at 50K comments/month -> worst-case Pro ~$9/month. Target gross margin 80%.

calendarEvents.title: Globex: security & roadmap review
calendarEvents.agenda: Globex security review: SAML/Okta enforcement, audit logs and retention, AI data handling, timeline.

attachments.title: Globex security questionnaire (answers draft)
attachments.body:
SSO: in development (Okta, Azure AD). Audit logs: logins, exports, role/settings changes, deletions; 1-year retention; CSV + API export.
Data: US-hosted, encrypted at rest and in transit. AI provider: no training, no retention; emails and phone numbers redacted.
